name: Advanced Experimental Design Patterns
description: This module describes advanced patterns for experimental design intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.
content:
This module describes advanced patterns for experimental design intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When experimental design decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Measure before optimizing any experimental design bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. State assumptions about experimental design explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Keep experimental design changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
5. Before starting experimental design work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. Validate experimental design outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen experimental design approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. Document any non-obvious experimental design decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop experimental design edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic experimental design advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting experimental design assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of experimental design correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated experimental design concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about experimental design over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
